categories.main_business_segments: Amcor operates two reportable segments: Flexibles and Rigid Packaging. The Flexibles Segment develops and supplies flexible packaging globally with approximately 35,000 employees at 166 facilities in 37 countries, accounting for 76% of consolidated net sales in fiscal 2023. The Rigid Packaging Segment manufactures rigid packaging containers and related products in the Americas with approximately 5,000 employees at 52 facilities in 11 countries, accounting for 24% of consolidated net sales. The company also produces specialty cartons and closures.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Amcor leverages expertise across multiple packaging materials including paper, metal, plastic, recycled, and bio-based materials. The company invests approximately $100 million annually in research and development, with more than 1,000 active patents and a global network of Innovation Centers. Core capabilities include flexible and rigid packaging manufacturing, specialty carton production, and closure manufacturing using advanced packaging technologies and sustainable material science.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Amcor serves diverse end markets including food, beverage, pharmaceutical, medical device, home and personal care, and other consumer goods industries. The company has no single customer exceeding 10% of consolidated net sales. Primary customers are major consumer goods and healthcare companies globally. The company operates across Europe, North America, Latin America, Africa, and Asia Pacific regions.
categories.geographic_coverage: Amcor operates globally with significant presence in Europe (30% of employees), North America (30%), Latin America (20%), and Asia Pacific (20%). The company has 218 locations in over 40 countries. In fiscal 2023, approximately 74% of sales came from developed markets and 26% from emerging markets including Argentina, Brazil, China, Colombia, India, and Peru.
categories.supply_chain_position: Amcor operates primarily in the midstream to downstream segments of the packaging supply chain. The company manufactures and supplies primary packaging directly to consumer goods and healthcare companies. Raw materials including polymer resins, films, paper, inks, solvents, adhesives, aluminum, and chemicals are sourced from global suppliers, with the company not significantly dependent on any single supplier.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Amcor's strategy focuses on three components: a focused portfolio of primary packaging businesses, differentiated capabilities through 'The Amcor Way' (Talent, Commercial Excellence, Operational Leadership, Innovation, and Cash Discipline), and aspiration to be the leading global packaging company. Key R&D priorities include sustainable packaging innovation, developing recycled and bio-based materials, advancing circular economy solutions, and achieving science-based net zero emissions targets by 2050.
categories.revenue_model: Amcor generates revenue primarily through direct sales of packaging products to customers. The company sells flexible packaging, rigid packaging containers, specialty cartons, and closures through a direct sales force supported by product development engineers and customer service teams. Revenue is recognized at the point in time when control of packaging products is transferred to customers upon shipment.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include AptarGroup, Ball Corporation, Berry Global Group, CCL Industries, Crown Holdings, Graphic Packaging, Huhtamaki, International Paper, Mayr-Melnhof Karton, O-I Glass, Sealed Air, Silgan Holdings, Sonoco Products, and WestRock. Amcor considers itself a significant participant in its markets, though precise competitive positioning is not readily determinable due to business diversity. Competition focuses on price, innovation, sustainability, quality, and service.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Amcor is a large accelerated filer with approximately $14.7 billion in net sales for fiscal 2023, representing 1% growth compared to fiscal 2022. Net income attributable to Amcor plc was $1,048 million in fiscal 2023 compared to $805 million in fiscal 2022, a 30% increase. The company has approximately 41,000 employees globally and maintains investment-grade credit ratings. Diluted earnings per share increased 33% to $0.705 in fiscal 2023.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Amcor differentiates through innovation excellence, global packaging expertise, and commitment to responsible packaging solutions. The company offers a diverse portfolio of differentiated products addressing unique customer needs with technical know-how and business experience. Key differentiators include sustainability leadership (pledging all packaging recyclable, compostable, or reusable by 2025), extensive R&D capabilities, global scale and reach, and ability to provide cost-effective, functional, and environmentally responsible packaging solutions across multiple materials and formats.
